messages.author: Daniel Roe
messages.body:
Hi,
Here is the relevant error message:
> Unable to build internal Boost without zlib and libbz2
You need to either install the zlib or libbz2 development libraries,
or Boost itself. If you can't do that, you could try to disable Boost
and anything that depends on it via the cmake variable
-DDISABLE_TOOLS=Boost (I think, those more familiar with cmake may
want to chime in here).
-Dan

messages.author: David A Case
messages.body:
On Sun, Mar 24, 2024, ABDELATIF MESSAOUDI via AMBER wrote:
>
>I am trying to install AMBER22. After running "./run_cmake"
>I am getting the error :( Attached please find my error message)
Look in the cmake.log file for the phrase "CMake Error". Then right above
that is the origin of the problem:
>-- Unable to build internal Boost without zlib and libbz2
>CMake Error at cmake/3rdPartyTools.cmake:108 (message):
> 3rd party program boost is required to build Amber, but it is disabled
> (likely because it was not found).
You need to install zlib and libbz2. See
https://ambermd.org/Installation.php
, and choose your OS.
...good luck...dac

messages.author: David A Case
messages.body:
On Mon, Mar 25, 2024, ABDELATIF MESSAOUDI wrote:
>Dear David
>
>Which file can I add these :
>-DDISABLE_TOOLS=Boost
>-DFORCE_DISABLE_LIBS="boost".
>
>I really need to install Amber22 on my new machin
The above won't work. You need to install the zlib or libz2 libraries.
Exactly how you do this depends on your OS: please visit
https://ambermd.org/Installation.php
. For example, on Linux Ubuntu, the
required command is this:
sudo apt-get install libz-dev libbz2-dev
Find the page for your operating system.
...dac

messages.author: David A Case
messages.body:
On Mon, Mar 25, 2024, ABDELATIF MESSAOUDI via AMBER wrote:
>
>I am trying to install AMBER22. After running "./run_cmake"
Did you edit the run_cmake script? Are you trying to use Intel compilers?
>/home/lcmvar/SOFT/amber22_src/build/AmberTools/src/pysander/CMakeFiles/pysander-build/temp.linux-x86_64-cpython-312/sander/src/pysandermodule.o
>error: command 'icc' failed: No such file or directory
Possible workarounds:
Use GNU compilers (the default); Intel compilers should not be needed
except for rare (and advanced) situations
If the first idea fails, try adding -DDISABLE_TOOLS="pysander" to your
run_cmake script.
...good luck...dac
